Theme

Clothes & getting dressed

coat noun

also overcoat, topcoat

classical

Traupman 116

paenula, paenulae f.

noun, first declension

In ancient Latin a travelling cloak.

Other words

  • amiculum, amiculī n. — coat, mantle

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Traupman 116; M-O s.v. jacket, coat: coat; Cic.

  • superindūmentum, superindūmentī n. — overcoat

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Traupman 117, 396; M-O s.v. jacket, coat: overcoat; Tertullian (ecclesiastical); Traupman 118

  • paenula cucullāta — hooded coat

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. jacket, coat: coat with a hood

  • palliolum, palliolī n. — a little cloak

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut.; Juv.

    Our word for a child’s coat.

  • amīcula, amīculae f. — a little girlfriend (not a coat)

    noun, first declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 293

    Traupman prints amicula -ae f for coat; that is the diminutive of amīca (Lewis & Short s.v. amīculus). The garment is amiculum, neuter, with a short i.

Examples

  • Theodōrus, excitātus, paenulam prīmum sēnsit, deinde frīgus per paenulam

    When Theo woke up, he felt first his coat, then the cold through the coatcomposed

  • Onerā palliolō umerōs tuōs.

    Put your little coat on.after Pont. Progymn. I 2

See also raincoat, jacket, cloak, hood, sweater.
